did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hezekiah began to reign at the age of twenty-five and reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was named Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
Did you know? In the first year of his reign, in the first month, Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.

Did you know? Hezekiah described how the Temple had been neglected: the doors of the vestibule were shut, the lamps had been extinguished, incense had not been burned, and burnt offerings had not been presented.
Did you know? Among the Levites who undertook to purify the Temple were representatives of the Kohathite, Merarite, and Gershonite families, as well as descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun.

Did you know? The purification of the house of the Lord began on the first day of the first month and was completed on the sixteenth day—after eight days of work in the vestibule and another eight days in the Temple.
Did you know? The Temple furnishings that King Ahaz had discarded during his reign were restored, consecrated, and placed before the altar of the Lord.
Did you know? Hezekiah ordered the sacrifice of seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats to make atonement for the kingdom, the Temple, and Judah.
Did you know? The restoration of Temple worship also included music: the Levites played cymbals, harps, and lyres, while the priests blew the trumpets.

Did you know? The people brought seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs for burnt offerings; in addition, they brought six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep and goats as sacred offerings.
Did you know? Hezekiah and the people rejoiced because the worship of the house of the Lord had been restored so quickly; the text emphasizes that it happened suddenly.
